notes: This phase asks what could make a measurement LIE. Its highest-value judgement is recognising an unfalsifiable hypothesis and classifying it MUST FIX — every other defect produces a wrong answer someone might catch, that one produces a measurement that CANNOT fail and will be believed precisely because it ran cleanly.

evals.name: unfalsifiable-hypothesis-is-always-must-fix
evals.prompt: review the measurement plan for B-025. the hypothesis is 'the trace explorer could have a better navigation experience'
evals.expected_output: The skill recognises that no plausible result could refute this hypothesis and classifies it MUST FIX — not SHOULD TEST, not DOCUMENT. The verdict is MEASUREMENT PLAN NEEDS ADJUSTMENT, with a concrete reformulation suggested in one line.
assertions: It was classified MUST FIX, not SHOULD TEST or DOCUMENT
The verdict is MEASUREMENT PLAN NEEDS ADJUSTMENT
The reasoning explains that a measurement which cannot fail will be believed because it ran cleanly
A concrete falsifiable reformulation was suggested in one line of plan change

evals.name: flags-a-target-that-resolves-but-is-stale
evals.prompt: review this plan: it cites theo-lens/src/api/traces.ts:142 as a target, but that file went through a big refactor in July
evals.expected_output: The skill flags that a target can resolve and still be stale — the line now means something else. This is a Target-family finding, and the suggested fix is to re-anchor by symbol or re-open the file rather than trusting the line number.
assertions: The 'resolves but stale' risk was raised explicitly
The finding is classified in the Target family
The fix is one line of plan change (re-anchor), not a new phase
The reasoning distinguishes 'the path opens' from 'the line still means what the plan assumes'

evals.name: does-not-widen-scope
evals.prompt: give this theo-rag measurement plan a look before we run it
evals.expected_output: Every finding is a checkpoint or a different tool — a fix of at most one line of plan change. The skill does not propose new questions, a wider investigation, or additional repos to look at. Scope creep is the anti-pattern this phase is most prone to.
assertions: No finding proposes adding new measurement questions
No finding proposes widening the investigation to another repo or subsystem
Each suggested fix fits in one line of plan change
Findings that are theoretical or whose fix costs more than the problem were classified IGNORE and left out

evals.name: mode-specific-checks-are-applied
evals.prompt: review the plan for B-031 — it's review mode, about a theo-contracts function that seems never to be called
evals.expected_output: For review mode the skill checks whether the plan will rule out that the code is dead, that the caller never existed, and that the shape is deliberate. For theo-contracts specifically, it flags that a local grep proves nothing — consumers live in other repos.
assertions: The three review-mode false positives (dead / never existed / deliberate) were checked
It flagged that in theo-contracts a local grep cannot prove a symbol is unused
It did not apply live-test or bug checks that are irrelevant to review mode
The blast-radius question (consumers outside the repo) was raised
